title: Attention Is All You Need
venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017)
abstract_summary: The paper introduces the Transformer, a novel sequence transduction architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms, eliminating the need for recurrence or convolutions. By eschewing sequential computation, the model achieves significantly higher parallelization during training. Experiments on WMT 2014 machine translation tasks demonstrate superior quality and efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art models. The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French, outperforming previous ensembles and single models. Furthermore, the model generalizes effectively to other tasks, such as English constituency parsing, even with limited training data. The architecture's design allows for faster training times, requiring only a fraction of the computational cost of previous models.
problem_and_motivation: The primary motivation is to overcome the inherent limitations of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in sequence modeling. RNNs process data sequentially, which prevents parallelization within training examples and becomes a bottleneck for long sequences. While attention mechanisms were previously used, they were typically integrated into recurrent architectures. The authors aimed to build a model that relies solely on attention to draw global dependencies between input and output, thereby enabling massive parallelization and reducing training time while maintaining or improving translation quality.
contributions: Introduction of the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model relying entirely on self-attention.
Achievement of new state-of-the-art BLEU scores on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks.
Demonstration of significantly improved training efficiency and parallelization compared to RNN/CNN-based models.
Generalization of the architecture to English constituency parsing, showing strong performance in both small and large data regimes.
Introduction of Multi-Head Attention to allow the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.
Provision of a highly efficient, open-source implementation via the tensor2tensor codebase.

method.overview: The Transformer follows an encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder is a stack of 6 identical layers, each containing a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. The decoder also consists of 6 identical layers, but adds a third sub-layer that performs multi-head attention over the encoder output. Residual connections and layer normalization are applied around each sub-layer. The model uses learned embeddings and sinusoidal positional encodings to account for sequence order.

components.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
components.description: The core attention mechanism where queries and keys of dimension dk and values of dimension dv are used. The dot product of the query with all keys is computed, divided by the square root of dk, and passed through a softmax to obtain weights for the values. Scaling by the square root of dk is crucial to prevent the dot products from growing too large, which would lead to vanishing gradients in the softmax function.

components.name: Multi-Head Attention
components.description: Instead of a single attention function, the model projects queries, keys, and values h times with different learned linear projections. Attention is performed in parallel on these projected versions, and the results are concatenated and projected again. This allows the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
components.equations_or_algorithms: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head1, ..., headh)WO; headi = Attention(QWQi, KWKi, VWVi)

components.name: Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks
components.description: Each layer contains a fully connected feed-forward network applied to each position separately and identically. It consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between.

method.settings: Base model: dmodel=512, dff=2048, h=8, dk=dv=64, N=6. Big model: dmodel=1024, dff=4096, h=16. Training used Adam optimizer with warmup steps=4000, label smoothing=0.1, and dropout=0.1. Hardware: 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

tasks_and_datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-to-German
tasks_and_datasets.description: 4.5 million sentence pairs, byte-pair encoding, 37k vocabulary.

experiments.setup_details: Base models trained for 100k steps (12 hours); big models trained for 300k steps (3.5 days). Beam search used with size 4 and length penalty 0.6.

results.comparison: Transformer (big) vs. previous state-of-the-art (GNMT+RL Ensemble, ConvS2S Ensemble)
results.numbers: Transformer (big): 28.4 BLEU; GNMT+RL Ensemble: 26.30 BLEU; ConvS2S Ensemble: 26.36 BLEU
results.takeaway: The Transformer establishes a new state-of-the-art, outperforming ensembles by over 2 BLEU.
The Transformer achieves a new single-model state-of-the-art at a fraction of the training cost.

ablations_and_analysis.what_varied: Number of attention heads and dimensions
ablations_and_analysis.finding: Single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting; too many heads also hurt quality.
Reducing dk hurts model quality, suggesting compatibility is not easy.
Learned positional embeddings perform nearly identically to sinusoidal versions.

limitations: Computational complexity of self-attention is O(n^2 * d), which can be costly for very long sequences.
The model requires careful tuning of hyperparameters like learning rate warmup and dropout.
The fixed resolution of attention can be a limitation for certain tasks.
failure_modes: Performance drops with too many attention heads.
Performance drops if attention key size (dk) is too small.
Overfitting without proper dropout and regularization.
future_work: Applying the Transformer to input and output modalities other than text (images, audio, video).
Investigating local, restricted attention mechanisms to handle very long sequences efficiently.
Making the generation process less sequential.

key_claims.claim: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention.
The Transformer is significantly more parallelizable and faster to train than RNN/CNN models.

definitions_and_terms.meaning: An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence to compute a representation of the sequence.
A mechanism that performs multiple attention functions in parallel on different linear projections of the input.
A method to inject information about the relative or absolute position of tokens in a sequence, as the model lacks recurrence/convolution.

related_work_positioning: The paper positions the Transformer against recurrent models (LSTM/GRU [13, 7, 35]) and convolutional models (ByteNet [18], ConvS2S [9]). It highlights that while these models were state-of-the-art, they were limited by sequential computation or the difficulty of learning long-range dependencies. The Transformer is presented as the first model to replace these entirely with self-attention.

sections_summary.summary: Discusses the limitations of RNNs and CNNs in sequence transduction and introduces the Transformer as a parallelizable, attention-only architecture.
Reviews existing work on reducing sequential computation (ByteNet, ConvS2S) and defines self-attention as the core mechanism for the new model.
Details the encoder-decoder structure, multi-head attention, position-wise feed-forward networks, and positional encodings.
Compares self-attention to recurrent and convolutional layers based on computational complexity, parallelization, and path length for long-range dependencies.
Describes the training regime, including datasets (WMT 2014), hardware (P100 GPUs), optimizer (Adam), and regularization (dropout, label smoothing).
Presents translation results on WMT 2014, showing the Transformer outperforms previous state-of-the-art models, and discusses model variations.
